subject: biochemistry
title: Glycolysis, pyruvate dehydrogenase and the tricarboxylic acid cycle

steps.tx: The **glycolytic pathway** in the cytoplasm converts one molecule of glucose into two molecules of pyruvate with the net generation of two ATP and two NADH. The commitment step is catalyzed by phosphofructokinase-one, which phosphorylates fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. Phosphofructokinase-one is allosterically inhibited by high cellular ATP and citrate, and powerfully activated by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate, synthesized by the tandem bifunctional enzyme PFK-2.
steps.say: The glycolytic pathway converts one molecule of glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, generating two ATP and two NADH. The rate-limiting step is catalyzed by phosphofructokinase-one, converting fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. It is inhibited by ATP and citrate, and activated by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate.

steps.tx: The mitochondrial **pyruvate dehydrogenase complex** bridges glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid cycle by oxidatively decarboxylating pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, releasing carbon dioxide and generating NADH. It requires five essential cofactors: thiamine pyrophosphate (vitamin B1), lipoic acid, coenzyme A (pantothenate B5), flavin adenine dinucleotide (riboflavin B2) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (niacin B3). Thiamine deficiency impairs PDH, causing lactic acidosis and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
steps.say: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex bridges glycolysis and the citric acid cycle by decarboxylating pyruvate to acetyl-CoA. It requires five cofactors: thiamine pyrophosphate, lipoic acid, coenzyme A, FAD and NAD+. Thiamine deficiency impairs the enzyme complex, causing lactic acidosis and Wernicke encephalopathy.

steps.tx: The **tricarboxylic acid cycle** or Krebs cycle oxidizes acetyl-CoA within the mitochondrial matrix, producing three NADH, one FADH2, one GTP and two carbon dioxide per acetyl-CoA turned. Oxaloacetate condenses with acetyl-CoA via citrate synthase to form citrate. Isocitrate dehydrogenase catalyzes the rate-limiting oxidative decarboxylation to alpha-ketoglutarate, inhibited by ATP and NADH and activated by ADP. Succinate dehydrogenase embeds directly within inner mitochondrial complex two.
steps.say: The tricarboxylic acid cycle oxidizes acetyl-CoA within the mitochondrial matrix, producing three NADH, one FADH2, one GTP and two carbon dioxide per turn. Citrate synthase condenses oxaloacetate with acetyl-CoA. Isocitrate dehydrogenase is the rate-limiting step, inhibited by ATP and activated by ADP. Succinate dehydrogenase is inner mitochondrial complex two.

steps.tx: Arsenic poisoning directly inhibits the pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes by binding the sulfhydryl groups of **lipoic acid**. This disrupts aerobic mitochondrial respiration and ATP synthesis, producing vomiting, rice-water diarrhea, garlic-scented breath and prolonged QT interval. Fluoroacetate inhibits aconitase, while malonate acts as a classical competitive inhibitor of succinate dehydrogenase, arresting cycle progression.
steps.say: Arsenic poisoning inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase by binding lipoic acid sulfhydryls. This disrupts mitochondrial ATP synthesis, producing vomiting, rice-water diarrhea and garlic breath. Fluoroacetate inhibits aconitase, while malonate inhibits succinate dehydrogenase.
